title: Reintroduce stream-range-tags and fncall-handshake for SSE atomicity
author: Arielle Chen
release_notes: Fixes rare partial-JSON emissions when SSE chunk boundaries split function-call/structured-output spans. Adds stream-range-tags (in-band lightweight start/end offsets) and a fncall-handshake to guarantee atomic delivery of function call sentinels and argument objects across fragmented chunks. Backwards compatible; gated by feature-flag and rolled out gradually.
description: Context and motivation: We continued to see intermittent customer reports (SUP-4421) of corrupted or truncated JSON objects emitted from the SSE-compatible streaming path when requests hit network-level chunking boundaries while a function/tool-call was being streamed. Existing heuristics (delimiter coalescing + trailing-escape rewrite) mitigated many cases but left a low-frequency class of failures where the tool-call sentinel and the JSON payload were split across noncontiguous chunks, causing downstream parsers to observe partial JSON and drop the fncall. Summary of change: Introduce two orthogonal safeguards: 1) stream-range-tags: a lightweight in-band start/end range marker attached to SSE frames that carries minimal offsets and an idempotency token. These tags let the client-side parser quickly determine whether a logical JSON span is complete or in-progress and support safe reassembly when chunks are re-ordered by proxies. 2) fncall-handshake: a tiny handshake protocol layered on top of the existing SSE events for function/tool calls. The producer emits a "fncall:pre" event with a short opaque token and the receiver responds (ACK) before the full argument object is emitted; if the consumer cannot ACK (or ACKs with NACK), the producer will buffer and re-emit the argument object with the same token until acknowledged or until a soft timeout. Implementation notes: - Minimal runtime changes in streaming core: stream-range-tags are encoded as additional SSE-meta headers (non-user-visible) and carried through the stream coalescer and backpressure path. - Parser updates in the OpenAI compatibility layer: the SSE lexer now understands range-tags and associates them with the next data event; fncall-handshake is implemented as a corner case in the structured-output serializer. - Feature gating: default-off in prod, controlled by config `stream.sse.range_tags` and `stream.sse.fncall_handshake`. Rollout plan: enable serverside support behind flags, run integration tests and internal canary against the streaming playground, enable for 10% of hosted API traffic for 48h, monitor structured-output error rate and client-side parse failures, then ramp to 100%. Backwards compatibility: if the client doesn't understand range-tags or handshake events the runtime will fall back to the legacy delimiter coalescer; tags are ignored by older clients. Testing and verification: - Unit tests: parser and lexer coverage for split-chunk cases (UTF-8 boundary, delimiter-in-middle). - Integration tests: end-to-end harness that injects deliberate chunking/reordering at the proxy layer. - Chaos testing: high-concurrency chaos run with synthetic chunk drops and replays. Observability and metrics: added `sse.range_tag.missed_spans`, `sse.fncall.handshake_failures`, and `sse.fncall.handshake_latency` to track behavior during rollout. Security/compat: range-tags carry no customer PII and the handshake tokens are short opaque values; no extra auth surface. Performance: microbenchmarks show <=1.5% p99 latency impact for small payloads; batching unchanged for common cases. Rollback: flip feature flags off to restore legacy behavior. Related: references ENG-9123, SUP-4421. Next steps: consider an optional client-side library helper to interpret range-tags when present to further reduce parse-side reassembly work.

review_comments: Samir: Can you quantify the perf impact on median/p99 for small (<=1KB) responses? I'm worried the extra meta will inflate token sizes.
Arielle (response): Microbenchmarks attached to the CI run show median unchanged, p99 <=+1.5% for small payloads; added a comment and benchmark artifact to the PR.
Jordan: The fncall-handshake makes the consumer responsible for ACKing—are we exposing a new API contract? How does this affect third-party proxies?

Arielle (response): The handshake is optional and internal to the SSE stream; we don't change the public HTTP surface. Proxies that only pass bytes will be unaffected; clients that understand the handshake can ACK to allow earlier resource reclamation. Added compatibility note and fallback behavior in docs.
Maya: Please ensure tokens are rotated and not predictable; also add metrics for handshake failures so we can detect regressions during rollout.
Arielle (response): Switched to cryptographically strong 64-bit opaque tokens and added `sse.fncall.handshake_failures` metric. Tests updated.

Deploy runtime change to dedicated staging and run canary tests for 24h
Schedule 10% rollout and monitor sse.* metrics for 48h
